title: Design LRU Cache with TTL
description:
Design an LRU cache `TTLLRUCache` where each stored entry also has a **time-to-live (TTL)**:
- `TTLLRUCache(int capacity)` initializes the cache with positive `capacity`.
- `int get(int key, int timestamp)` returns the value of `key` if it exists and has **not expired** (`timestamp < expireAt`), marking `key` as the most recently used entry (without changing its `expireAt`). If `key` does not exist or has expired (`timestamp >= expireAt`), remove it if present and return `-1`.
- `void put(int key, int value, int timestamp, int ttl)` inserts or updates `key` with `value`, sets its expiration time to `expireAt = timestamp + ttl`, and marks it as most recently used. Before evicting any live entry when at capacity, purge all expired entries (`expireAt <= timestamp`); if the cache is still at capacity after purging expired entries, evict the least recently used live entry.

Timestamps across all calls are guaranteed to be non-decreasing.
constraints: At most 2000 calls will be made to get and put.
hints: Combine a standard LRU doubly linked list + hash map with a min-heap keyed by `(expireAt, version, key)`.

Before executing `get` or `put` at `timestamp`, pop every heap entry with `expireAt <= timestamp` and unlink the corresponding node from the DLL if its `version` still matches (lazy invalidation for updated keys).

examples.explanation: Key 1 expires at t=6, so get(1,5)=10 succeeds while get(1,6)=-1; put(3,30,7,5) purges expired key 1 so key 2 is not evicted.
Neither key expires, so get(1,3) refreshes key 1 and put(3,3,4,100) evicts the LRU key 2.
Updating key 1 at t=4 refreshes both its value to 99 and its expiration to 4+10=14.
